objectives.text: Money services businesses are subject to the program requirements set forth and cross referenced in this subpart.

citations.quote: Money services businesses are subject to the program requirements set forth and cross referenced in this subpart.

objectives.text: An effective anti-money laundering program is one that is reasonably designed to prevent the money services business from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities.

citations.quote: An effective anti-money laundering program is one that is reasonably designed to prevent the money services business from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities.

obligations.action: develop, implement, and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program

citations.quote: shall develop, implement, and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.

obligations.action: make the AML program's design commensurate with the risks posed by the location and size of, and the nature and volume of the financial services provided by, the business

citations.quote: The program shall be commensurate with the risks posed by the location and size of, and the nature and volume of the financial services provided by, the money services business.

obligations.action: maintain the AML program in writing

citations.quote: The program shall be in writing, and a money services business shall make copies of the anti-money laundering program available for inspection to the Department of the Treasury upon request.

obligations.action: make copies of the anti-money laundering program available for inspection to the Department of the Treasury

citations.quote: The program shall be in writing, and a money services business shall make copies of the anti-money laundering program available for inspection to the Department of the Treasury upon request.

obligations.action: incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to assure compliance with this chapter, at a minimum

citations.quote: Incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably designed to assure compliance with this chapter.

obligations.actor: provider or seller of prepaid access (that is a money services business)
obligations.action: establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains prepaid access under a prepaid program and obtain identifying information (name, date of birth, address, identification number)
obligations.trigger: a person obtains prepaid access under a prepaid program

citations.quote: A money services business that is a provider or seller of prepaid access must establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains prepaid access under a prepaid program and obtain identifying information concerning such a person, including name, date of birth, address, and identification number.

obligations.action: establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains prepaid access to funds and obtain identifying information (name, date of birth, address, identification number)
obligations.trigger: person obtains prepaid access to funds
obligations.threshold: funds that exceed $10,000 during any one day

citations.quote: Sellers of prepaid access must also establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains prepaid access to funds that exceed $10,000 during any one day and obtain identifying information concerning such a person, including name, date of birth, address, and identification number.

obligations.trigger: last use of the prepaid access device or vehicle
obligations.threshold: five years after the last use

citations.quote: Providers of prepaid access must retain access to such identifying information for five years after the last use of the prepaid access device or vehicle; such information obtained by sellers of prepaid access must be retained for five years from the date of the sale of the prepaid access device or vehicle.

obligations.trigger: date of the sale of the prepaid access device or vehicle
obligations.threshold: five years from the date of sale

citations.quote: Providers of prepaid access must retain access to such identifying information for five years after the last use of the prepaid access device or vehicle; such information obtained by sellers of prepaid access must be retained for five years from the date of the sale of the prepaid access device or vehicle.

obligations.action: designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and this chapter

citations.quote: Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program and this chapter.

obligations.action: provide education and/or training of appropriate personnel concerning their responsibilities under the program, including training in the detection of suspicious transactions to the extent reporting is required

citations.quote: Provide education and/or training of appropriate personnel concerning their responsibilities under the program, including training in the detection of suspicious transactions to the extent that the money services business is required to report such transactions under this chapter.

obligations.action: provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program, with scope and frequency commensurate with risk; reviewer may be an officer or employee who is not the person designated under paragraph (d)(2)
exceptions: review may be conducted by an officer or employee of the money services business so long as the reviewer is not the person designated in paragraph (d)(2)

citations.quote: Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate program.
The scope and frequency of the review shall be commensurate with the risk of the financial services provided by the money services business.

obligations.action: develop and implement an anti-money laundering program that complies with the requirements of this section
obligations.threshold: on or before the later of July 24, 2002, and the end of the 90-day period beginning on the day following the date the business is established

citations.quote: A money services business must develop and implement an anti-money laundering program that complies with the requirements of this section on or before the later of July 24, 2002, and the end of the 90-day period beginning on the day following the date the business is established.

obligations.actor: agent-only money services business and its principal money services business
obligations.action: may by agreement allocate between them responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls required by paragraph (d)(1)
obligations.trigger: person is a money services business solely because it is an agent under § 1022.380(a)(3)

citations.quote: may by agreement allocate between them responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls required by this paragraph (d)(1).

obligations.action: remain solely responsible for implementation of the requirements of this section notwithstanding any allocation agreement with an agent

citations.quote: Each money services business shall remain solely responsible for implementation of the requirements set forth in this section, and nothing in this paragraph (d)(1) relieves any money services business from its obligation to establish and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.

obligations.actor: money services business with automated data processing systems
obligations.action: integrate compliance procedures with such automated data processing systems

citations.quote: Money services businesses that have automated data processing systems should integrate their compliance procedures with such systems.

interactions.description: MSB program-requirements subpart directs users also to the general (cross-sector) program requirements of 31 CFR part 1010, subpart B, which apply to money services businesses.

citations.quote: Money services businesses should also refer to subpart B of part 1010 of this chapter for program requirements contained in that subpart which apply to money services businesses.

interactions.description: Definitions section of Part 1022 defers to the general definitions of Part 1010 for terms not separately defined in Part 1022, including the definition of 'money services business' itself.

citations.quote: Refer to § 1010.100 of this chapter for general definitions not noted herein.

interactions.description: The agent-allocation provision for AML program policies/procedures/internal controls cross-references the agent status/registration-exemption provision in § 1022.380(a)(3).

citations.quote: A person that is a money services business solely because it is an agent for another money services business as set forth in § 1022.380(a)(3), and the money services business for which it serves as agent, may by agreement allocate between them responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls required by this paragraph (d)(1).

notes: Extraction is confined to the AML program/'pillars' establishment obligations for money services businesses in 31 CFR 1022 Subpart B (§§1022.200, 1022.210), consistent with ratified scope. Subparts C (Reports/SARs), D (Records), and E/F (information sharing, special standards/measures) are treated as coordination-layer or boundary material (SAR/CTR/CDD operational duties; recordkeeping) and are excluded from the obligation table per the ratified scope, though §1022.380 (registration) was likewise excluded as a non-'program' BSA duty; these sections are noted only where directly cross-referenced from the Programs subpart. The text mixes 'shall' and 'must' within the same section (e.g., §1022.210(a) uses 'shall'; §1022.210(d)(1)(iv) uses 'must' for prepaid-access provisions); both are preserved as written and mapped to modality 'must' without harmonizing the verb choice, per the fidelity rule. The agent-allocation clause in §1022.210(d)(1)(iii) uses permissive 'may' for allocating responsibility while simultaneously imposing a non-relievable 'shall remain solely responsible' duty on each MSB; this internal tension is preserved as written (see O14/O15) rather than resolved. Cross-reference quotes retain the source's literal HTML entity rendering (e.g., '§') exactly as it appears in the provided source text, per the verbatim-quote requirement.
